answer: Because the ivory index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the tundra audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 161 answers need 161 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the delta identifier and voids the later submissions, and as a result the operator burns for 161 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
